registered_before: the probe change exists and any data with program identity is recorded
owner_decisions: 24/11: do B2 of improvement-round-2 (program identity of exec sessions, a session model per program)
24/11: B3 (Kubernetes pods/exec audit) last, after the model is fixed, as the rule comparison (with and without)
idea: a session process (entered by a runtime exec, and its descendants) carries the name of the program it executed (the task's comm right after a successful execve, inherited at fork); the session part of a window is scored per program by a model of that program learnt from normal operations (exec probes and routine operator commands), and by the pooled session model (S1a) when the program has too little learning data. A routine command already seen is then judged against its own past behaviour; a new program falls back to the pooled model as in S1a

probe.change: pulse_task_state gains prog: on a successful execve return of a session-lineage thread, prog = a 15-bit FNV-1a hash of the 16-byte comm (never 0), and the comm is stored once in a new map pulse_prog_names (hash -> comm); fork copies prog; native threads keep prog 0. The gram key's pad = lineage | prog << 1. The loader keeps 'grams' and 'session' as before (summed over programs) and adds 'session_prog': [[t0,t1,t2,t3,count,prog], ...] plus a 'prog_names' line for every new hash
probe.checks: the token proof (one token per syscall) and the lineage proof must pass on the three workers; the overhead A/B of token-probe-overhead-v1 (getpid, read, futex, open+close, mmap+munmap, forkwait) against the final build must show no added cost beyond the 95 % interval of the earlier comparisons

routine_operations: during the A1 capture (two diurnal days) a routine operator runs, about every 10 min at a seeded random time, one command of the routine set in a seeded random production container through kubectl exec: find, grep, sleep, stat, wc (five of the nine v6 operator commands other than ls_tmp, chosen by sha256('exec-identity-v1:' + name) rank; ls_tmp is left out because the living-off-the-land step uses ls). Held out: head, hostname, printenv, whoami (and ls_tmp). These are normal operations and are learnt
learning: session models per program name from the session_prog part of the capture's windows (minimum 200 learning blocks per program, else the pooled session model), cross-fit and Gumbel rule as the pooled session model at alpha' 0.00015
evaluation: on the one final live run (alert path S1a; the program identity recorded), offline: S1a against S1a+B2 on the same windows: operator commands flagged for the routine set and for the held-out set; attack, lotl and event-generator recall (primary >= 95 %, PAD 300, on-off, 0.1 and 0.5 per s >= 95 % each, lotl and event generator >= 95 %), idle control <= 5 %, burden per regime. B2 is reported as a learnt mechanism measured on the final run; it is not on that run's alert path
limits: comm is the program name (16 bytes), not a verified identity: an attacker who names its binary like a routine command is scored by that command's model
operator commands are simulated by a schedule; real operator behaviour varies more
the datasets have no runtime exec, so B2 does not change LID-DS or CB-DS
